title: "Does the reconstruction match the three-quarter store photograph?"

::: {#9977b983 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
ENTRY_CEILING = 120.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 250.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 179.4      # s the probe actually used

import re
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Camera seed for the front-port three-quarter perspective
hint_threequarter = (24.2, 227.0, 2.1)
rgb_overlay, pose_note = compare_to_photo(airplane, "threequarter", hint=hint_threequarter)

# Parse fitted camera pose and outline residual
m_pose = re.search(
    r"elev ([0-9.]+)° azim ([0-9.]+)° roll ([-0-9.]+)°, ([0-9.]+) px/m\. Fit: ([0-9.]+) px, ([0-9.]+)%",
    pose_note,
)
elev_fit = float(m_pose.group(1))
azim_fit = float(m_pose.group(2))
roll_fit = float(m_pose.group(3))
scale_fit = float(m_pose.group(4))
fit_px = float(m_pose.group(5))
fit_pct = float(m_pose.group(6))
```

::: {.hero}

**Answer.** Partially. As confirmed in the [tolerance check](2026-10-05-01-can-we-reconstruct-the-ft-tubby-b-17-within-tolerance.qmd), fuselage length ([1168 mm]{.key}) and tractor nacelle stations match the photograph closely (@fig-threequarter-overlay), with the inboard nacelles placed forward of the outboards. The silhouette fit reaches [1\.8%]{.key} ([19\.5 px]{.key}) at camera elevation [23\.9°]{.key} and azimuth [225\.7°]{.key}. However, wing chord and taper show a distinct mismatch: the physical wing trailing edge extends well aft of the reconstructed outline along the entire outer panel, indicating the true wing has a broader chord and rounded tip than the modeled taper.
